newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wired magazine dumps German partners to go solo.
newsitem.headline: Wired magazine dumps German partners to go solo.

text.p: The publishers of Wired magazine, considered the hippest of an entire generation of Internet-related journals, said on Thursday they had dumped their local partners to go it alone and set up a German-language issue.
"Our original intent was to put out the German issue together with the publishers Spiegel and Gruner + Jahr," said Louis Rossetto, founder and manager of Wired magazine.
"Differing views over the responsibilities of the chief editor (of the German issue) made this partnership impossible."
Wired Ventures, Inc, Spiegel Verlag, publisher of Germany's biggest weekly news magazine, and Gruner + Jahr, the country's largest magazine publisher, formed a partnership in June.
A spokesman for Gruner + Jahr said the talks with Wired broke down over a number of issues, including the basic concept for the German-language magazine and questions of personnel.
The German partners now appear to be considering whether to launch a similar publication of their own.
"This cannot be ruled out. We will talk about this," said Gruner + Jahr spokesman Christoph Groffy.

Wired, with circulation of more than 300,000 copies, is the biggest-selling magazine in the United States covering technological, social, cultural and regulatory issues related to the Internet, the global computer network.
In addition to its U.S. publication, there are local issues of Wired in Britain and Japan. The German issue is expected to be available next year.

It also operates HotWired, an online publication on the World Wide Web, the fast-growing graphical part of the Internet, and produces television films about cyberspace and operates a book publisher, HardWired.
